messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: Dedicated pool 'eu-west-2' reporting p99=8.2s (> SLO 2s) for last 10m, streaming stalls observed. queue_depth=42, warmup_delay=~35s. Auto-scale attempted but warmup lagged. Ticket INC-2026-451 created.

oncall-aaron: acked. jumping on now. trying to reproduce. any customer-visible errors?

customer-ops-maya: several VIP customers reported timeouts and partial streams, support ticket #CS-9820 opened. severity elevated.

sre-zoe: seeing tail spikes correlate with coldpool handshakes. probes show large tail latency on hotshot requests during bursts.

runtime-alyssa: logs show repeated kv-cache misses and model init warmup taking ~28-40s. snippet: 
```
WARN runtime: model warmup incomplete after 30s
stream: stall at token 0 - waiting for KV population
metric queue_len=42, warmup_last=2026-03-16T20:58:12Z
```

platform-sam: autoscaler shows scale-up started at +12s but pods not READY until +40s due to nvlib init. infra ticket suggests driver coldstart.

oncall-aaron: immediate mitigation options? fallback to non-streaming (buffered) for affected routes? route to smaller quantized model?

eng-raj: we can flip routing to rdx-small-quant for non-critical traffic. that cuts perf but reduces warmup. recommend throttling burst clients down 20% while we stabilize.

runtime-alyssa: quick commands: 
```bash
# check pod readiness
kubectl get pods -l pool=dedicated-eu-west-2 -o wide
# force warmup probe on new pods
curl -X POST https://internal-api/serve/warmup?model=rdx-base
```

sre-zoe: bumped capacity by enabling reserved-hotshots (manual) - started 3 hot pods, but still seeing tail due to pending KV populate. pushing a prefix-fill job.

platform-sam: routing rule applied: 15% of traffic -> rdx-small-quant, 10% rate-limit on known burst clients. dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/incident/INC-2026-451 (lv: latency, qd: queue_depth).

oncall-aaron: customers impacted estimate? Maya?

customer-ops-maya: ~7 customers with degraded streaming, 2 enterprise customers saw >30% request failures for 12m. CS escalations in flight.

eng-raj: created a short-lived canary: spin a warm pool with pre-populated KV for top prefixes. should cut p99. launching now.

incident-bot: NOTE: cache-prefill job started (job-id jf-881).

sre-zoe: after prefill p99 dropped to ~1.6s for test traffic. production trending down but still noisy.

oncall-aaron: moving to handoff soon. will keep routing adjustments for next 30m. oncall-beth, you're up next, see summary below.

oncall-beth: thanks -- I'll take it. please paste quick remediation steps and customer list.

oncall-aaron: TL;DR: cause = dedicated pool saturation + autoscale warmup lag (driver + kv-population). mitigations applied: 1) route 15% -> rdx-small-quant, 2) rate-limit burst clients 10%, 3) manual hot pod spawns x3, 4) triggered cache-prefill job jf-881. monitor p95/p99 and streaming success.

oncall-aaron: customer list: (CS-9820) Acme Corp, (CS-9823) NovaApps, (CS-9827) Finlytics -- CS owning comms.

oncall-beth: got it. I'll watch dashboards and escalate to infra if p99 > 2s for another 10m. taking over incident channel.

customer-ops-maya: continuing comms to affected customers, ETA updates in ticket.

eng-raj: follow-up: we should add warmup-prefill to autoscale workflow and consider lighter quant variants for hotshot fallback. filing RFC-1752.

platform-sam: noted. infra follow-up on GPU driver coldstart scheduled.

oncall-beth: handoff accepted. closing live mitigation window at 1713214700 for oncall-aaron. I'll keep thread updates. :white_check_mark:
